data.title: bn-2kr: Bundle static Lua modules with source provenance
data.description: Review static require tokenization, graph/path confinement, cycles/aliases, generated loader semantics and namespace isolation, nil/false caching, syntax/source maps, reports, tests, and docs. Full just check passed.

data.body: The previous-token check conflates a member-access `.` with the final byte of Lua concatenation `..`. Consequently valid code such as `local value = "prefix" .. require("foo")` skips the import entirely, produces a bundle without `foo`, and fails only at runtime. It also bypasses the promised dynamic-require rejection when the requested module is bundled by another literal import (for example `require("foo"); local name="foo"; local x="" .. require(name)`). Track punctuation as Lua tokens/operators rather than a single byte, distinguishing `.`, `..`, and `...`; add scanner plus build/runtime regressions for a require following concatenation (and ideally a direct call after a `::label::`, which the analogous colon heuristic also skips).

Syntax is validated only after raw module bodies have been inserted between generated factory delimiters. An unclosed block in a module can consume the generated `end`; the parser then reports an error on later glue outside every source-map range, so the documented original path/line remap is lost. Worse, two individually malformed sources can balance each other (for example module `a` ends with an unclosed `if`, while a later module body begins with an extra `end`), allowing the whole bundle to parse even though factory nesting and runtime loading are corrupted. Syntax-compile every entry/module body independently in an equivalent vararg-function/chunk context before emission, retain final-bundle validation, and add regressions for missing `end` provenance and cross-module delimiter balancing.

One adjacent lexer regression is worth covering while this is open: Lua 5.4 permits `\\z` in a short string to consume following whitespace, including newlines, but `skip_short_string` skips only the `z` and then reports the legal newline as an unterminated string. This affects unrelated strings, not just module literals. Please teach the scanner that escape form or explicitly establish a narrower supported-Lua contract (the current docs say Lua 5.4).

data.reason: Static-import scanning misclassifies require after Lua operators/labels and misses dynamic calls, and whole-bundle-only syntax validation allows module bodies to consume generated delimiters while losing source provenance (threads th-3mavsr and th-3g4e35). Focused existing tests pass.

data.body: Fixed in f59513c. Every entry is syntax-compiled independently as a chunk and every module as an equivalent variadic factory before graph emission; final bundle validation remains. Errors report canonical source/module/line. Added a regression using the exact missing-end/extra-end cross-boundary shape plus wrapper-context unit coverage; just check passes.

Fixed in 623c4c3 and f59513c. The scanner now tokenizes .., ..., and :: distinctly from member/method punctuation, and implements Lua 5.4 \z whitespace consumption. Scanner coverage and a full build/runtime regression exercise concatenation, label-adjacent require, and \z; just check passes.

data.reason: Fixed across 623c4c3 and f59513c: scanner distinguishes concatenation/vararg and label delimiters from member/method punctuation, consumes Lua 5.4 \\z whitespace with line tracking, and build/runtime coverage exercises all three contexts.

Fixed in f59513c: entry chunks and variadic module bodies are syntax-compiled independently before scanning/emission; the exact cross-module delimiter-balancing reproducer now fails with canonical source/module/line provenance, while final bundle validation remains.
Re-reviewed f59513c. Both blocking defects are fixed with meaningful scanner, build/runtime, and cross-boundary syntax regressions; focused project tests, reference coverage, and diff hygiene pass.
